notes:
Account background: Aurora builds a workflow automation SaaS for mid-market product teams (in-app assistants, automated triage). Recently experienced multiple latency regressions with incumbent LLM provider that started affecting live chat agents (spikes at p95). Decision: evaluate migration to Redwood — starting with Hosted API (fast onboarding) during POC, then move to Dedicated capacity if latency and cost targets met.

POC summary / timeline:
- 2025-11-05: Intro call (Maya) — product & infra overview; customer prioritized streaming and tool-calling.
- 2025-11-12: NDA signed; shared initial data samples and prompt templates.
- 2025-12-03: Baseline bench (incumbent) run by Aurora infra team — observed 180-450ms per-token tail jitter under load; p95 ~820ms for user-turns when connectors called external DBs.
- 2026-01-08: Redwood hosted POC kickoff — seeded with 50k tokens/day test traffic, streaming websocket enabled; tool-calling stubs for search + internal CRM. (fireflies: ff_20260118_initial_intro)
- 2026-01-22: First Redwood vs incumbent benchmark: Redwood streaming showed more consistent token throughput and lower tail; internal summary: median token latency improved ~30-40ms, p95 user-turn ~350-480ms depending on turn length.
- 2026-02-12: Deep-dive review with SE (Carlos) — demoed streaming + function-calling; Redwood suggested KV prefix caching for repeated prompts, and batch window tuning. (fireflies: ff_20260212_aurora_poc_review)
- 2026-02-20: Customer ran sustained 200 concurrent chat sessions simulation; Redwood hosted maintained latency SLO targets for p95 under 600ms for user-turns, whereas incumbent regressed beyond 900ms intermittently.
- 2026-02-25: Cost model review — Aurora asked for Dedicated pricing and expected unit cost target ~$0.003/token equivalent; requested quantization/instance recommendations.

Technical requirements / priorities (from CTO & infra lead):
- Latency SLO: p95 user-turn <600ms (including tool call round-trips); token-level streaming latency target <50ms where possible.
- Streaming + function-calling reliability: resume/partial responses, traceable invocation logs.
- Security: SOC2 compliance required, SSO via SAML, audit logs retained 1 year, KMS integration for key wrapping.
- Deployment preference: start hosted for speed, then Dedicated (VPC) for isolation and predictable throughput.

Why they're migrating: "We've seen intermittent regressions from our current vendor that broke streaming sessions and increased abandonment in product pilot customers" — quote from Head of Product. Cost creep + unpredictable tail latency are the main drivers.

POC artifacts requested by customer:
- Raw benchmark CSVs (latency per-token and user-turn) — provided by Aurora and Redwood SE.
- Pricing scenarios for 12/24 month committed Dedicated pools.
- VPC networking checklist and security addendum template.

Sales/Commercial notes:
- Customer is price-sensitive but prioritizes latency and reliability for their PLG growth motion.
- Likely to convert to Dedicated if Redwood can commit to predictable p95 targets and provide a clear migration playbook.
- Legal wants draft data residency clause and KMS/HSM integration terms before procurement.

Next steps (detailed):
- Deliver extended POC report (includes 2-week sustained load run) by 2026-03-05.
- Provide Dedicated SKUs and sample pricing deck tailored to Aurora usage profile.
- Arrange CISO call to walk through security FAQ and KMS options.
- Tech deep-dive on onboarding internal tool-calling connectors (SE + Aurora infra).

- "Want p95 <600ms for chat agent turn incl. tool calls."
